clue.text: Type of weapon that could ruin the service first

indicators.note: first tells the solver that the word for the church service is placed at the front, ahead of the word for ruin

blocks.note: Mass is the Eucharistic church service
ruin as a noun means wrecking or devastation

explanation.surface: A saboteur's weapon designed to wreck a church service before anything else happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' reads as a verb in the surface, but the wordplay wants it as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons of mass destruction are the nuclear, chemical and biological arms category named in treaties and news reports.

clue.text: Man's man, perhaps

blocks.note: surface reading: a man who enjoys male company, a blokeish type
setter's reading: Man is the Isle of Man, so a Man's man is someone from that place, one example of a particular kind of resident

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea; its people are Manx. Capitalised at the start, 'Man's' hides that it is the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man is an inhabitant of an island, so he is one example of an islander.

clue.text: Account makes bishop sick

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
sick means unwell

explanation.surface: Settling some account leaves a bishop feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a written statement of charges owed, the same as a restaurant or trading account.

clue.text: Lay claim to some of the woodwind, or other instruments

blocks.note: to bag something is to claim it for yourself, as in bagging a seat
pipes are simple woodwind instruments, a subset of that family

explanation.surface: A musician staking a claim to part of the woodwind section, or to some other instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other' is fair because bagpipes are not usually counted among orchestral woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes are reed instruments fed from an air bag, sounding through chanter and drones, so they qualify as musical instruments.

clue.text: Still playing Act 1 on the street

indicators.note: playing means performing freely with the letters, so the act and the numeral are scrambled
in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the street goes on top

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
Act taken as written, with 1 read as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Street performers are still doing the first act of their show out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Static describes something motionless or unchanging, exactly as an adjective still does.

clue.text: A crowned head, poetically in motion?

definitions.text: A crowned head, poetically in motion?

blocks.clueFragment: A crowned head, poetically in motion?
blocks.note: surface reading: a monarch moving about, described in verse
setter's reading: a poet crowned with laurel, a post then held by Andrew Motion

explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate when this ran, so the capital-less 'motion' hides his surname. The title means one crowned with laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: The title derives from the Latin for wreathed in laurel, the crown given to honoured poets, and Motion then held it.

clue.text: Testing place for two-piece ensemble

blocks.note: first meaning: the Pacific atoll where the US tested nuclear bombs
second meaning: a woman's two-piece swimsuit

explanation.surface: A changing room where you can try on a two-piece outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimsuit was named after the atoll, days after the 1946 bomb tests there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshall Islands atoll hosted American nuclear trials, and the same name labels the skimpy two-part swimwear.

clue.text: Moving call?

blocks.note: surface reading: an emotional, touching phone conversation or appeal
setter's reading: moving means portable, a device for calls that travels with you

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' suggests emotion; read literally it means able to move about, which describes a portable phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellphone is carried around, so it is a portable instrument for making calls on the move.

clue.text: An assault involved one replacing you, it's said, as the aggressor

indicators.note: it's said points to a single letter whose spoken name matches the word you
replacing means one letter is swapped out and another put in its place
involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are jumbled together

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: A police report on an assault, noting which party was the aggressor.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the U in AN ASSAULT for I, then rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks another, which makes them the aggressor in a fight.

clue.text: Leave after French friend finds a Spanish one

indicators.note: after places the word for depart behind the French word, at the end

blocks.note: ami is French for friend
go means leave or depart

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a French pal and takes up with a Spanish one instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' in the definition stands for friend, borrowed from earlier in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the ordinary Spanish word for a pal or companion, widely borrowed into English.

clue.text: Seafood used to make curves round the edge

blocks.note: first meaning: a bivalve shellfish eaten as a delicacy
second meaning: to cut a border into a series of rounded segments

explanation.surface: A chef uses shellfish to decorate the rim of a plate in a wavy pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish has a fan-shaped ribbed shell, and its wavy outline gave the verb for cutting decorative curved borders.

clue.text: They are the end of the line for interim alterations

definitions.text: They are the end of the line

indicators.note: alterations are changes, so the letters of the word before it are changed in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Temporary changes to a railway timetable bring services to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are terminal stations, where rail or bus routes finish, literally the final stops on a route.

clue.text: Donkey losing its head in a whirl

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the animal's name is dropped

blocks.note: neddy is a British informal word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A beheaded donkey sent spinning, a gruesome comic image.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling circular current of water or air, so it is a small whirl or vortex.

clue.text: Become an authority on a Spice Isle, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the phrase might be rearranged into something else

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar who aims to become the expert on one of the tropical Spice Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: To specialise is to concentrate study on a narrow field until you become an expert in it.

clue.text: Quarrels about a king's charges

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for quarrels wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: tiffs are petty quarrels
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Rows break out over the fees a monarch imposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are the duties or price lists levied on goods and services, so they are a kind of charge.

clue.text: Birdman disturbed once between rivers

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up
between puts the jumbled word inside the two river names around it

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher once upset while standing between two streams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rivers' supplies two: the Cornish Fal at the front and the abbreviation R at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer keeps and trains hawks and falcons for hunting, so he is a man who works with birds.

clue.text: Cause a capital loss

blocks.note: surface reading: bring about a financial loss of invested money
setter's reading: capital means relating to the head, so a capital loss is losing one's head

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like finance; capital punishment and decapitation point to the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone to death, especially by beheading, is to make them lose their head.

clue.text: Brussels official finds carer out

indicators.note: out means disordered or off course, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; out is both part of the letters and the signal

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat in Brussels discovers a care worker is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: All eight letters of 'carer out' are rearranged, so 'out' does double duty as letters and as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocrat is an administrator in the European Union's institutions, which are headquartered in Brussels.

clue.text: One line in vague duties could be put to some purpose

indicators.note: vague means unclear and ill-defined, so the following word's letters are blurred into a new order
in places the numeral and the abbreviation inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single line in an unclear job description could serve some purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Utilised means made use of, which is to employ something or put it to a purpose.

clue.text: Coverage of model, plus theory

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters that follow are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Reporting that covers a scientific model and the theory behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun in the surface, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstery is the padding and fabric that covers sofas and chairs, a kind of coverage for furniture.

clue.text: Also coming up the girl's nose

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom upward, so the word for also goes backwards
up as in inside, so the turned word is lodged within the word for the girl's

blocks.note: her is the possessive for a girl
too means also

explanation.surface: Something else is going up a girl's nose, a schoolyard image.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooter is British slang for a nose, especially a large one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooter is informal British slang for the nose, named from the honking noise of blowing it.

clue.text: The new church is from that direction

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A newly built church faces in that direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Thence is an old-fashioned adverb meaning from that place, so it describes coming out of that direction.

clue.text: Refer to it in church

indicators.note: in places the little pronoun inside the abbreviation for the church

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to mention something during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote or mention a source as evidence, which means to refer to it.

clue.text: Any small number first for the match

indicators.note: first tells the solver to put the small number at the front, ahead of the word for any

blocks.note: two is a small number
any and some are interchangeable, as in have you any or some

explanation.surface: Any small team will do as the opening side for the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A match can mean a well-suited couple, and a twosome is a pair of people together.

clue.text: Report has it that Mrs Blair's husband gets love

indicators.note: report has it means as heard spoken, so a name's sound stands in for its spelling

blocks.note: Cherie Blair is the wife of the former Prime Minister Tony Blair
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Gossip that Tony Blair receives affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Cherie Blair is the wife of Tony Blair, UK Prime Minister 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to hold them dear and treat them tenderly, which is to love them.

clue.text: Happening not to finish level

indicators.note: not to finish means the final letter of the word is left off

blocks.note: an event is a happening or occurrence

explanation.surface: A race that is going to end in a dead heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and level both describe a flat surface or scores that are equal, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: The honour initially seems empty, but carries a lot of weight

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each of the next two words is kept

blocks.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
the opening letter of seems
the opening letter of empty

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that an honour looks hollow yet is still very influential.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour given by the monarch. 'Empty' looks like a removal signal but just supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obese is very overweight, so they literally carry a lot of weight around.

clue.text: Henry came round to sign note on environmentally sensitive species

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the verb for arrived wraps around the king's abbreviation
on means placed after in an across answer, so the sign and note follow

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Henry turned up to put his name to a memo about protecting an endangered species.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a man's name but is the physics unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes colour to match its surroundings, so it responds to its environment, a witty description of the lizard.
